chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā al-Muʿādhī, from al-Ṭayālisī, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “When your supposition always goes toward completion in every salat (prayer), then perform two sajdahs without rukuʿ. Have you understood?” I said: “Yes.”

As for the last report which included mention of salat al-fajr, it may be understood as referring to what we mentioned earlier regarding the nawafil, and it may also be understood that this report is specific to one who prayed and thought that he had prayed two rakʿahs, then became certain that he had prayed only one rakʿah. In that case, he adds another rakʿah to it, and repeating the salat (prayer) is not obligatory upon him. Repetition is only obligatory upon one who doubts in it, so that he does not know whether he prayed one rakʿah or two, and that has not become clear to him; then at that point repeating the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him. What clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.سَجْدَتَيْنِ: the two sajdahs to be performed for forgetfulness
key_terms.وَهْمُكَ: your supposition or mistaken impression regarding the state of the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts the number of rakʿahs in salat al-fajr?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings concerning forgetfulness and doubt in salat (prayer), especially in relation to thinking the prayer is complete and the case of salat al-fajr. It distinguishes between one who later becomes certain of having prayed only one rakʿah and may complete the prayer, and one whose doubt remains unresolved, in which case repeating the salat (prayer) is required.
